verdicts.note: Raw HTML fetched with a browser UA (HTTP 200, 87,140 bytes), tags stripped. The 'How does this work?' modal, under 'Tips for the Analysis Tool', carries both limbs: the analysis is optimised for creative writing and essays, and may work for other domains but will likely under-report slop. Authorship attribution rests on the same panel's source-code link to github.com/sam-paech/slop-score (the page names no author in prose).

arXiv PDF 2203.15721v1 fetched and text-extracted (pdftotext -layout). Abstract carries the quoted words contiguously in 'the nature of the diversity-quality trade-off in language generation is very task-specific'; the 'rather than a property of the decoding rule' limb is supported by the abstract's opening ('the properties elicited by various decoding strategies do not always transfer across natural language generation tasks') and by the Discussion.

verdicts.trueWording: for all tasks besides SG, we see repet
verdicts.note: PDF page-6 column break confirmed: the line ends 'we see repet-' and continues 'itive behaviour in less than 1% of generations.' in section 5, Repetitions. SG is story generation; the other tasks are MT, AS, Diag and ULG.

Table 5 ('Perplexities and repetition count for different strategies on the SG task'), Story Gen. (small) '% repetition' column: Greedy 95.67, Reference 0 — both figures exact. The Reference row is the human-written WRITINGPROMPTS continuation (Table 1 names the dataset; section 5.1 calls the row 'human generated references'). Claim carries no quotation; the figures match verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: little consistency across tasks in terms of
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'across a set of generations' — the sentence attributes the inconsistency to SEQUENCE-level string diversity, and the same paragraph reports set-level diversity as consistent across tasks
verdicts.note: The quotation is verbatim in section 5.2, but the sentence completes 'sequence-level string diversity.' The two sentences immediately before it say the opposite of the claim for set-level diversity: 'For diversity metrics calculated over a set of generations, ancestral sampling consistently generates the most diverse text' and 'Mode-seeking decoding strategies consistently have a stronger negative correlation with set-level diversity metrics'. Section 4.1.2 defines the paper's two levels (string level, within a string; set level, across strings), so the claim's 'across a set of generations' names the level the page reports as consistent. The 'Interestingly' that opens the sentence marks it as the contrast to that consistency.

arXiv PDF 2210.15191v1. Table 4 ('repetition-degeneration rates ... in an adversarial setting'), column lg: top-p 47%, eta-sampling (ours) 26% — exact. Section 5.4's prose repeats both figures for GPT-2 large. The injected repetition is the paper's synthetic corruption: the last 3 subword tokens repeated 5 additional times. Claim carries no quotation; the figures match verbatim.

Section 5.4, Setting: 'We take natural prompts—the first 35 words of the Wikipedia biographies of the 101 people with the most-read Wikipedia pages'. 'Opening words' = the first 35 words; 'stress test' is the paper's own word ('To stress test the methods, we devise an adversarial setting').

Section 5.2, Results: the line-wrapped 'pre-/ferred over top-p (53% to 40%)' is verbatim. Raters were 59 US Mechanical Turk Masters judging which 70-token suffix follows a 35-token prefix, so 'continuations' holds. Note the paper's prose attaches 53/40 to Study 1 while Table 3 gives Study 1 as 39%/53% and Study 2 as 40%/53%/6% equal; the claim's pair of figures appears verbatim in the prose and exactly in the Study 2 row.

verdicts.trueWording: less critical after the model is aligned
verdicts.note: arXiv PDF 2402.06925v3, section 4.1, under the heading 'Aligned models are less dependent on decoding methods than unaligned models'. The narrowing limb is carried by the MBPP example: unaligned Llama2-7B spans 21.20% (FSD-d) to 7.80% (mirostat), the aligned Chat model 21.60% to 16.00%, 'showcasing a narrowed performance range'. The paper qualifies the generalisation — relative deviation is lower for the aligned model on every dataset except XSUM and CNN/DM, where the two are close.

Table 2 ('The entropy of Llama2-7B and Llama2-Chat-7B's generation results (top-p sampling with p = 1.0) on GSM8K, MBPP and Wikinews'), Wikinews column: Llama2-7B 2.37, Llama2-7B-Chat 0.52 — exact. Section 4.1 calls it 'the average next-token prediction entropy'. Claim carries no quotation; the figures match verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: the aligned model produces much fewer repetitions
verdicts.note: Section 4.1, 'Phenomenon Analysis', reason ii ('The alleviated degeneration issue'): the sentence continues 'even when using deterministic decoding methods such as greedy search', and the passage is explicitly one of three 'potential reasons' for the narrowed decoder gap, so the 'partly' limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: it is orthogonal to the decoding strategy
verdicts.note: arXiv PDF 2510.01171v4 (stamped 15 Jul 2026), Appendix F.3 'Ablation on Decoding Strategies': the quoted words are verbatim, and the next sentence names the layering — temperature, top-p, and min-p sampling. Section 5.1 repeats it ('VS is orthogonal to these generation parameters and can be combined with them').
Abstract: 'For instance, in creative writing, VS increases diversity by 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting.' Quotation verbatim; both limbs (creative writing, over direct prompting) on the same sentence.

Table 2 ('Human-rated diversity (1 = Very Similar, 4 = Very Dissimilar) for poem, story, and joke tasks'), Story row: Direct 2.74, VS-Standard 3.06 — exact. Section 5.2 supplies the study limbs: 'a human study on Prolific', 'We recruited 90 annotators (30 per task)', '4-point Likert scales'. Claim carries no quotation; the figures match verbatim.

verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'at every stage they tested ... and RLVR' — the paper records diversity drops after SFT and DPO only; the (SFT, RLHF, RLVR) list qualifies where VS improves diversity, not where diversity falls
verdicts.note: The quotation is verbatim across the line-wrapped hyphen in section 5.1: 'Figure 4 in Section F.1 confirms that post-training reduces output di-/versity, and VS improves diversity across all post-training stages (SFT, RLHF, RLVR).' The parenthetical attaches to VS's improvement. Figure 4's caption states 'Baseline prompting methods experience major diversity drops (mode collapse) after SFT and DPO', and Appendix F.1 gives direct prompting 20.8% after SFT falling to 10.8% after DPO; no drop is stated or numbered for the RLVR stage (Tulu-Final-70B), which the caption uses to show VS holding diversity. So the reduction is established for SFT and RLHF/DPO, not confirmed stage-by-stage through RLVR.
